title: Sheet Pan Chicken Trays
seoTitle: Sheet Pan Chicken Trays | Firefighter Meal
subtitle: Portioned trays, reheat-ready
description: Portioned trays, reheat-ready. Sized for a full crew, with timing that still works when the kitchen gets interrupted.

steps.title: Heat oven and prep pans
steps.instruction: Preheat 425°F. Toss chicken and veg with oil and seasoning on two rimmed pans — single layer only or you'll steam.

steps.title: Roast until charred
steps.instruction: Roast 18–22 minutes, swap racks halfway, until chicken reads 165°F and peppers have blistered edges.

steps.title: Serve family-style
steps.instruction: Pile Sheet Pan Chicken Trays onto trays. Hold backup pan foil-covered at 200°F. Squeeze lime at the line if using.

steps.title: Batch the next pan
steps.instruction: While the crew eats, start a second batch on clean pans if you're feeding stragglers. Scrape burned bits — they smoke up the hall.

proTips: Cool portions in shallow trays before the fridge — deep containers stay in the danger zone too long.
Keep a backup tray warm in the oven for late calls — nothing worse than cold protein after a run.
Taste for salt at the end — hall palates run salty after long shifts.
Pull chicken at 160°F and let carryover hit 165°F — dry breast ruins crew morale.
tonightSpread: Plate Sheet Pan Chicken Trays with sides in separate pans so the crew can mix portions.
Line up Sheet Pan Chicken Trays on the main counter with serving spoons — firefighters grab fast between calls.
Keep a backup tray warm in the oven at 200°F for late arrivals after a run.
leftovers: Cool leftovers in shallow containers within two hours — deep pots stay hot too long.
Label trays with date and reheat to 165°F minimum before second shift.
Portion into individual containers on night one — locker-friendly for shift two.
whyCrewsLikeIt: Portioned trays, reheat-ready. A hall pick for regular dinner nights — one line, real portions, no drama at the stove.
mealPrepNotes: Cook protein and sauce ahead; assemble day-of in under 20 minutes. Label and date everything in the fridge.
substitutions: Chicken thighs ↔ breasts (thighs forgive overcooking on the flat-top).
